name: Axiom Systems Perimeter Denial System PDS-4 'Cordon'
description:
A modular area-denial weapon system consisting of ground-mounted directional mine units that fire high-velocity ball bearings in a pre-set arc when triggered by sensor input. Each Cordon unit covers a 90-degree arc to a depth of 200 meters, and units are designed to be chained together to create continuous perimeter coverage.

Axiom Systems designed the PDS-4 for unmanned perimeter defense where budget constraints prohibit autonomous turrets or human guards. Each unit costs less than a day's wages for a security guard, making the Cordon the most cost-effective lethal perimeter defense available. The units are weatherproof, require no power supply (using a chemical propellant charge), and remain armed for up to five years without maintenance.

The Cordon's simplicity is both its strength and its weakness. The units cannot distinguish between threats and civilians — they fire when their passive infrared sensor detects a thermal signature within their activation zone. Axiom's instruction manual recommends 'adequate signage' to warn unauthorized personnel.
legality: Licensed — property defense; Prohibited in public-access areas
specifications: caliber: 8mm steel ball bearings, 400 per unit effective_range: 10-200 meters in 90-degree arc rate_of_fire: Single instantaneous discharge capacity: 400 ball bearings per unit (single use) weight: 4.2 kg per unit power_source: Chemical propellant charge — no external power
tactical_use: The Cordon is deployed as a low-cost perimeter defense for warehouses, corporate facilities, and restricted zones where continuous human monitoring is impractical. Units are typically buried or concealed along approach routes and triggered autonomously when their thermal sensor detects intrusion. Four units arranged in a square create a complete perimeter defense that can deny access to an area without any human oversight.
cultural_context: The PDS-4 has become the most controversial weapon in GLMZ due to the frequency of civilian casualties. Lower-tier communities near corporate facilities have learned to watch for the Cordon's distinctive camouflaged housing, and informal mine-clearing networks have formed to identify and disable units placed in public spaces. Axiom's response to civilian casualty reports is invariably the same: 'The perimeter was clearly marked. Unauthorized entry constitutes assumed risk.'
story_hooks: A child was killed by a Cordon unit while playing near a corporate warehouse. The signage was in a language the community doesn't speak. The community is demanding justice, and someone is organizing a systematic campaign to locate and disable every PDS-4 in the lower tiers.
Someone has begun stealing Cordon units from corporate perimeters and redeploying them to protect squatter communities. The units are now pointing outward from homes instead of corporate facilities.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, squat cylindrical pod resembling a stubby concrete-anchored mine or autonomous sentry emplacement. Low-profile design meant to be partially buried or concealed. Top-mounted sensor array gives it a watchful, predatory appearance despite its stationary nature.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 18cm (above ground) | Diameter: 22cm | Buried depth: 10-15cm typical | Mounting base: 30×30cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively dense. 4.2kg feels substantial for its size — the heft of industrial engineering and propellant payload concentrated in a small footprint.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite (lower housing), hardened steel (internal firing mechanism and ball bearing magazine), aluminum heat sink collar
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical gray with powder-coat weatherproofing. Upper sensor dome in black anodized aluminum. Mounting base shows bare steel or rust-preventative coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate gray primary with black sensor cap. Accent strips in Axiom Systems corporate orange-red along the equipment ID band. Weathered appearance with micro-abrasion marks.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not handheld — textured grip ridges molded into the cylindrical sides for field handling during emplacement. Top-mounted carrying handle in reinforced polymer.
distinctive_features: Prominent passive infrared sensor dome mounted on top — dark, convex, slightly recessed
Radial blast ports arranged in a 90-degree forward arc — small openings suggesting high-velocity dispersal pattern
Serial number and 'LIVE PERIMETER' warning stencils on sides in reflective white paint
Chemical propellant ignition indicator (small pin or witness mark visible from top)
Axiom Systems corporate logo (triangular geometric form) stamped into metal nameplate
Thermal expansion vents as fine linear grooves around the mid-body
Mounting points for chaining adjacent units together (recessed flanges, rust-resistant bolts)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS logo and 'PDS-4 CORDON' designation stamped into aluminum nameplate on upper body. Serial number, manufacture date, and 'LICENSED LETHAL SYSTEM' warning in three languages molded into base plate.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-deployed units show weathering — salt spray oxidation on exposed steel, micro-scratches in polymer from deployment impact, sensor dome occasionally dust-hazed. Well-maintained corporate installations appear almost pristine; neglected perimeter deployments show rust bloom and algae growth on exposed surfaces.
